claimed_purpose.text: Official MCP reference server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory): persist a local knowledge graph (entities, atomic observations, typed relations) in JSONL and expose CRUD/search tools over stdio so a host model can remember project and user context across sessions.

mechanisms.text: Store: curated graph in MEMORY_FILE_PATH (default memory.jsonl); observations are one fact per line, not a raw chat transcript.

Retrieve: MCP tools (read_graph, search_nodes, open_nodes); README ships a system prompt that tells the model to open with "Remembering..." and pull relevant graph context at session start—selection is model-driven, not server-ranked.

Write: create_entities (skips duplicate names), create_relations, add_observations; delete_entities (cascade relations), delete_observations, delete_relations; no supersession or merge for conflicting facts.
Durability: in-process mutation queue plus temp-file rename on save; isolation is effectively one file per deployment/path, not multi-tenant.

Operational risks from issues: packaged server ignoring MEMORY_FILE_PATH; multi-process writers on one file losing updates; very large graphs making full read_graph costly; tool/schema bugs breaking writes.

ledger.claim: Atomic write via temp-file + rename prevents partial-write corruption on crash or power loss
ledger.quote: rename(2) is atomic on POSIX filesystems: readers see either the complete old file or the complete new one, never a partial state.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Concurrent mutation safety via serialised promise queue; issue #1819 documents the lost-update bug this fixes
ledger.quote: Serializes all read-modify-write graph mutations behind a single queue. Without this, concurrent tool calls (e.g. multiple mutations dispatched from one LLM turn) each independently load the graph, mutate their own copy, and write it back — so whichever write lands last silently overwrites the other's changes, and interleaved writes to the same file can corrupt it outright. See #1819.
ledger.label: measured

contested.text: README documents create_entities ignoring existing entity names; user reports and issues describe duplicate entities, failed adds, or JSON parse failures—treat idempotency and write reliability as contested in the field.
Docs and Docker examples assume MEMORY_FILE_PATH controls the store; issues report the published npm package not honoring env-based paths (wrong default file location).

Per-process write mutex prevents corruption within one server instance; issue #4797 reports two processes on the same path silently discarding each other's writes—multi-client safety is not guaranteed.

Bundled system prompt prescribes always retrieve at chat start; hosts that omit or override that prompt may behave as on-demand tool use only—continuity is co-owned by client integration, not enforced by the server.

copy.text: Agent/workspace memory primitive for MCP hosts (coding assistants), not a consumer companion product; human-like continuity depends on the client model following the README system prompt and calling tools consistently.

refuse.text: Do not treat issue #3400's 'create twice produces duplicate entities' as canonical behavior; README and index.ts skip duplicate entity names—use code/docs for idempotency, issues only for client/runtime failures.
Refuse unbounded read_graph on every turn at large graph sizes (issue #2415); companion-style continuity needs selective retrieve, not dumping 80k+ tokens of graph JSON.
Refuse multi-client write sharing on one MEMORY_FILE_PATH without external locking; per-process queue does not coordinate across processes (#4797).
